title: tests-green.sh runs the project's tests under `uv run` inside the target directory when pyproject.toml exists
spec:
Why: .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh (line with `command -v pytest ... else run python3 -m unittest discover -q tests`) uses whatever python3 is on PATH. Outside the MCP server that is the system Python 3.9 (no tomllib); inside the server it is the MAIN checkout's venv, which lacks dependencies that a task worktree added (T-0023 added scrapling, so merge()'s gate fails with ImportError even though the worktree's own venv is green). Gotchas 2026-09-17 in memory.

What (2 files: .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh, tests/test_orchestrator.py). This is a hook file; edit it in this worktree (the protected path is the main checkout only).
1. In the Python branch: if `command -v uv` succeeds and `pyproject.toml` exists in the target dir, run `uv run --project . python -m unittest discover -q tests` (cwd is already the target dir after the `cd`), preferring `uv run --project . pytest -q -x --no-header -p no:cacheprovider` when `uv run --project . python -c "import pytest"` succeeds. Keep the current pytest/python3 fallbacks when uv is absent. Set `UV_NO_SYNC` unset so uv syncs the worktree's venv from its own lockfile on first run (that is desired: a task that adds a dependency must be testable). Keep the failures-only output and loop-guard behaviour unchanged.
2. tests/test_orchestrator.py Hooks.test_tests_green_failures_only currently runs with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin (no uv) — keep it. Add one test: a scratch project with pyproject.toml and a test that imports a module only available in a per-project venv is hard to fake, so instead assert the script's chosen runner: run tests-green.sh with an env var `TESTS_GREEN_DRY=1` that makes the script print the runner command line and exit 0 (add this small dry-run switch at the top of the Python branch), and assert it contains `uv run --project .` when uv is on PATH and pyproject.toml exists, and `python3 -m unittest` when PATH lacks uv.

Run `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py`. Commit: "tests-green: run under uv inside the target project so worktree dependencies resolve" with a revert-path body.
acceptance: uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py exits 0 including the new dry-run test
with uv on PATH, `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh wt/<some worktree>` run from the main checkout uses that worktree's venv (dry-run shows uv run --project .)
without uv on PATH the old python3 -m unittest path is used (existing test still passes)
git diff --stat limited to .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh and tests/test_orchestrator.py

result.summary:
Working tree clean, commit in place on `task/T-0035`.

## Summary

Fixed `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh` so the Python test-runner branch prefers `uv run --project .` when `uv` is on PATH and the target dir has a `pyproject.toml` — this makes the gate use the worktree's own venv/lockfile (syncing it on first run) instead of whatever `python3` happens to be on the invoking process's PATH (previously the main checkout's venv when run from inside the MCP server, missing worktree-added deps like T-0023's `scrapling`). Falls back to the prior pytest/python3 behavior when uv is absent. Added a `TESTS_GREEN_DRY=1` switch that prints the chosen runner command and exits 0, used to test runner selection without needing a real per-project venv.

**Files changed:**
- `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh` — uv-aware runner selection + dry-run switch
- `tests/test_orchestrator.py` — new `test_tests_green_picks_uv_runner_when_available` test; fixed `MergeQueue.test_rebase_tests_ff_and_conflict`'s scratch `pyproject.toml` (needed a `version` field to be valid for `uv`, since real PATH now triggers the uv branch)

**Test output:** `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py` → `Ran 51 tests in 6.517s / OK` (no failures). `.claude/hooks/tests-green.sh .` run standalone also exits 0.

Committed as `09ef8d1` on `task/T-0035`. Diff is scoped to exactly the two allowed files.
